NDT training in Hobbs, NM: how it works for Hobbs employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Hobbs technicians and employers is self-paced online theory with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, followed by hands-on practice in person at the employer's own shop or field site. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Hobbs. The courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and your employer certifies you. We reply within one business day.

Hobbs sits on the New Mexico edge of the Permian Basin, and the local economy rises and falls with oil and gas activity. Wells, gathering lines, tank batteries, compressor stations and processing plants fill Lea County and the neighbouring counties, and each needs weld inspection when it is built and thickness checks as it ages.

Eastern New Mexico also has industries that are less obvious. Potash mining and processing, uranium enrichment and underground waste disposal all operate within a short drive, and all depend on documented inspection. A technician with a solid base in visual, magnetic particle and ultrasonic work can find openings across several of them.

How to get NDT certified in Hobbs: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

In Hobbs, certification in New Mexico follows the same pattern as elsewhere in the United States. In Hobbs, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies its own technicians, and the standard is a set of recommended practices that each employer turns into a written practice of its own. Here is the sequence in order.

  1. Find or have an employer with a written practice. A technician in Hobbs is certified by the company that employs them, so the first step is a sponsor whose written practice covers the method and level you want. In Hobbs, the practice sets the hours, the examinations and the recertification interval.
  2. In Hobbs, complete the formal training. Take the classroom hours the written practice requires. The training-requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours for each method, and your Hobbs employer may set higher figures.
  3. Log supervised experience. Document the hours a Hobbs technician spends performing the method under a certified Level II or III. Experience is usually the slowest part for a new Hobbs technician, so start the log from the first day on a job.
  4. In Hobbs, pass the general examination on principles, equipment and terminology for the method.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the procedures, equipment and acceptance standards your Hobbs employer really uses.
  6. In Hobbs, pass the practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner working under one.
  7. In Hobbs, pass the vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation at the intervals the written practice sets. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows what to expect.
  8. Receive certification signed by your Hobbs employer.
  9. In Hobbs, recertify at the interval the written practice sets, which SNT-TC-1A recommends should not exceed five years, by examination or documented performance as permitted.

In Hobbs, ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, and ASNT NDT Level III examinations) is the alternative if you want a credential that stays with you rather than with an employer. Atlantis prepares candidates for that route too. See ASNT certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Hobbs technicians

In Hobbs, each course follows the body of knowledge in SNT-TC-1A for its method. In Hobbs, level 1 courses cover the fundamentals and working under supervision, Level 2 courses cover setting up, calibrating, performing and evaluating examinations to a procedure, and Level 3 preparation covers the basic and method examinations for those who will write procedures and examine others.

In Hobbs, PAUT and TOFD are advanced ultrasonic techniques and are generally taken after UT Level II. In Hobbs, whether they can be used on a given job depends on the customer's specification and the employer's written practice.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Hobbs

Ultrasonic testing is the method a Hobbs technician reaches for once visual inspection is not enough. Level I training builds the fundamentals: how sound travels in steel, how to set up and calibrate the flaw detector, and how to take accurate thickness readings. Level II adds angle-beam weld examination, evaluation against the acceptance standard in the procedure, and reporting that another person can rely on.

In the Permian, produced water and sour service make internal corrosion a constant concern for tanks, separators and piping, and thickness monitoring is routine work. New construction brings its own demand, with weld examination on pipelines and facility piping. Use the Practical NDT simulator to rehearse scanning patterns and set-ups, read the course outline on the ultrasonic testing training page, and check your theory with the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Where NDT technicians work around Hobbs

Oil and gas production. Lea County is one of the busiest oil-producing counties in New Mexico. Operators and service companies maintain wells, flowlines, tank batteries and produced-water systems, and contractors there are often asked to show qualification records as part of operator onboarding.

Midstream and processing. Gas processing plants, compressor stations and the gathering and transmission pipelines linking them are a large source of inspection work. Piping and vessel work follows ASME B31.3 and B31.8 and API standards, and field welds are inspected visually and by radiography or ultrasonic methods depending on the specification.

Refining. The Navajo refinery in Artesia, within driving distance to the northwest, is one of the larger industrial facilities in southeastern New Mexico. Refineries run turnaround and in-service inspection programmes under API 510, 570 and 653, which employers may require inspectors to hold separately from NDT method certification.

Nuclear fuel cycle and waste. The Urenco USA enrichment plant near Eunice, in Lea County, and the Department of Energy's Waste Isolation Pilot Plant near Carlsbad are major employers with strict quality assurance programmes. Their contractors work to facility and nuclear quality requirements that go beyond a general SNT-TC-1A course, so the employer and its Level III set the qualification route.

Mining and fabrication. Potash mining and processing in the Carlsbad area, along with oilfield fabrication shops and welding contractors in Hobbs, add structural and equipment inspection.

For earnings information on Hobbs-area work, see our NDT salary guide, which cites public sources. Permian demand is cyclical, and technicians with several methods tend to ride out slow periods better.

NDT schools and classes near Hobbs: what to compare

NDT schools and classes near Hobbs are limited, and many technicians travel to Midland, Odessa or farther afield, or choose self-paced options. A classroom works for someone who can step away for a block of days and wants supervised time on specimens. Online theory works better for a working technician who rotates between sites, or for a company that wants to qualify field staff without long absences.

Compare providers on the questions that decide whether the training will help: does the provider certify you or does your employer, will the operator or plant owner accept the hours, who grades the practical, and is that person a Level III? Ask also whether the training will fit the written practice your employer already has, since contractor audits read that document and the records behind it.

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Hobbs. We offer online theory with Level III Q&A and the Practical NDT simulator, and the practical examination is done at the employer's facility. Our near-me guide explains how to approach employers about sponsorship, and the Permian Basin page covers the wider region.

Training a crew at your Hobbs facility

A Hobbs contractor with a group to qualify can run the entire programme at its own pace: self-paced online theory so crews keep working, then specific and practical examinations at your shop on your equipment and representative welds and piping. The specific examination can be written around the operator specifications and acceptance criteria your crews apply on the lease or in the plant.

Radiography licensing in New Mexico

New Mexico holds NRC Agreement State status. The New Mexico Environment Department's Radiation Control Bureau regulates radioactive materials and radiation machines, which covers industrial radiography. A radiography company working around Hobbs needs the state licence, and individual radiographers must satisfy its training, examination and supervision conditions. Federal facilities and some nuclear sites in the region operate under different authorities, so confirm which regulator applies to a given site. An RT course does not authorise anyone to use a source or license a radiographer. Employers normally need both radiation safety authorisation and SNT-TC-1A certification covering technique and interpretation. Verify current requirements with the Radiation Control Bureau.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Hobbs

How do I get NDT certified in Hobbs?

Be employed or sponsored by a company with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete its training and experience, pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and the employer certifies you.

Is there NDT work in Hobbs and Lea County?

Yes, mainly in oil and gas production, midstream, refining and facility construction, with some nuclear fuel cycle and mining work. Demand follows drilling activity, so ask operators and contractors directly.

Can I take NDT classes online in New Mexico?

Yes, the theory is online and self-paced. Practical training and the practical examination are hands-on with your employer.

Which method should I learn first for Permian work?

Visual weld inspection and ultrasonic thickness are the usual starting points, with magnetic particle and radiography added by many technicians.

How long is Level 2 training?

The employer's written practice sets the hours. See the training-requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended hours; experience usually takes longest.

Do I need API 510 or 570 as well?

Some employers also ask for API inspector certifications, which are separate from NDT method certification, and Atlantis does not teach them. Check what your target employer expects.

Can I get Level III training in Hobbs?

In Hobbs, yes, preparation is online and self-paced with Level III Q&A. See ASNT Level III training.

Does a course certify me?

No. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies. ASNT central certification is the alternative if you want a credential not tied to one employer.
